energy.question: Which generators, grid operators and equipment suppliers are delivering additional dependable power? Compare operation, financing, queues, cancellations and published outlooks beyond 2030.
What new supply, storage and clean-energy manufacturing is being delivered, by whom, where, and against which dated commitments?
Who pays for new power, grid and water infrastructure? Seek measured household bills, permits, water consumption and withdrawal, local benefits and adverse effects.
Which new developers, drilling suppliers and grid connections deliver geothermal power, and which constraints remain? Compare measured output with announced capacity.
Which operating fleets, restarts, new reactors and fuel-cycle suppliers change dependable power availability? Separate licensing, construction, operation and future targets.

chips.question: Which established or emerging designers, foundries, toolmakers, packaging and test suppliers expand real capacity? Preserve fab phase, node, location and shipment basis.
Which memory, storage, DSP, SerDes, copper, fiber, laser, module and co-packaged optics contributors remove or expose bottlenecks? Distinguish qualification from volume shipments.
What comparable revenue, capacity, yield, employment or equipment lead-time evidence reveals delivery, shortages or overcapacity? Keep revenue separate from funding and orders.
Which memory builders, equipment and materials suppliers expand qualified HBM, packaging and test supply? What evidence distinguishes shipped stacks, yields and usable capacity from announced plans?

Which photonics, DSP, laser, module, fiber and co-packaged optics contributors enable compute to scale within and across AI factories? Seek deployment and production evidence with costs and limitations.

infrastructure.question: Which owners, operators, regional clouds, builders and suppliers bring AI factories into service? Track site phases, energized IT capacity and delays without double counting.
Which contractors and training providers report actual paid work, wages, placements and shortages? Separate construction peaks, postings and permanent jobs.
What electrical, cooling and networking constraints or local procurement and fiscal outcomes matter? Seek public costs, tax incentives and household effects alongside receipts.

Which cooling and electrical suppliers change usable facility capacity, water use and energy efficiency? Seek measured operation, equipment delivery and bottlenecks rather than nominal product ratings.

Reconcile public operator location directories and newly named campuses against the complete accepted project catalog. Identify missing locations, aliases, ownership changes and delivery-stage gaps across regions. Include hyperscalers, neoclouds, sovereign AI and developers; familiar names are examples, not a coverage boundary.

Find overlooked large AI campuses and phase updates. Resolve Prometheus versus New Albany, Hyperion versus Richland Parish, Frontier versus Shackelford, and other aliases before proposing additions. Separate campus power, IT load, grid approvals, contracted capacity and actual energization. Never infer operation from a target year.

models.question: Which new or established open-weight and open-source builders, repositories and research groups contribute models or datasets? Verify checkpoint-specific license and availability; named incumbents are examples only.

What comparable capability, failure rate, latency, energy and accepted-work cost evidence exists across commercial and open models, languages and domains? Seek independent replication and regressions.
Which model builders, serving stacks and agent harnesses enable useful work? Track current releases, total costs, subscription conditions and human intervention without assuming successor names.

applications.question: Which companies and researchers demonstrate completed digital work beyond coding? Seek quality-adjusted productivity, adoption, new occupations, displacement and credible causal employment studies.
Which labs, hospitals and developers improve discovery, engineering, climate or medicine? Seek reproduced results, negative trials, safety and patient outcomes, not merely predictions or funding.
Which robotics, simulation, world-model and autonomous-system contributors show productive deployments? Preserve task-hours, interventions, uptime, safety, labor conditions and operating limits.

Which new groups demonstrate reproducible improvements in biology, chemistry, materials, mathematics or engineering? Distinguish open research resources, predictions, experimental validation and practical outcomes.

Which researchers and operational services improve weather, climate, clean-energy management or disaster preparedness? Seek independent verification, failure cases and real-world decisions rather than isolated benchmark wins.
